notes: Taejo of Goryeo, born Wang Geon, founded the Goryeo dynasty in 918 and completed the unification of the Later Three Kingdoms in 936.

Gustav II Adolf ruled Sweden from 1611 to 1632. He strengthened the Swedish state, reformed its army, and made Sweden a major European power during the Thirty Years' War. He was killed at the Battle of Lutzen in 1632.
Yasovarman I ruled the Khmer Empire from 889 to 910. He established Yasodharapura at Angkor and commissioned major hydraulic and temple works, including Phnom Bakheng.

Chulalongkorn (Rama V) ruled Siam from 1868 to 1910. He carried out administrative, legal, military, educational, and social reforms and helped preserve Siamese independence during the age of European imperialism.
Aung San Suu Kyi became a leading figure in Myanmar's pro-democracy movement in 1988 and served as State Counsellor from 2016 until the 2021 military coup.
